summary: Backend-only iteration 21 testing completed against the public preview URL. All core Client Portal Follow-up flows passed: optional field echo/list persistence, backwards-compatible intake creation, cookie-protected manual reminder errors and successful delivery metadata, cron Bearer auth/idempotency, 20h-32h selection, and all requested endpoint regressions. Three validation/security assertions failed: malformed appointment_at and signer_email values are accepted, and CORS still returns wildcard origin without credential support.

critical.issue: Input validation is absent for both new fields. The API returned HTTP 200 and persisted appointment_at='tomorrow around lunch' and signer_email='not-an-email-address'. These records silently cannot receive scheduled reminders.
Credentialed CORS contract fails: preflight returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and omits Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true instead of allowing the explicit app origin.

action_items: Change IntakeCreateIn.signer_email to EmailStr (while preserving empty/omitted compatibility) and validate appointment_at as an ISO datetime; reject malformed values with 422.

Normalize appointment_at to timezone-aware UTC before storage and comparison. The current frontend datetime-local value is timezone-naive while the cron window is UTC, so non-UTC appointments can be reminded at the wrong time.
Configure CORSMiddleware from explicit CORS_ORIGINS and set allow_credentials=True; wildcard origin cannot support cookie auth.
Retest intake validation, reminder selection with timezone offsets, and credentialed CORS after fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:162-163 models signer_email and appointment_at as plain strings; create_intake only strips them, so Pydantic provides no email or datetime validation.

routes/alerts.py:235-242 performs lexicographic string range queries against UTC ISO boundaries. Mixed offsets and the frontend's timezone-naive datetime-local strings are not chronologically safe; store a BSON datetime or one canonical UTC representation.
server.py:1990-1995 hardcodes allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=False, ignoring CORS_ORIGINS despite cookie-based authentication.
server.py remains approximately 2,000 lines, above the 700-line maintainability threshold; intake routes should be extracted into a focused router as alerts and invites were.

The requested /app/auth_testing.md playbook file is absent; credentials were available and the specified checks were implemented directly. Bcrypt $2b$, configured admin password, secure HttpOnly cookies, lockout after five failures, and the existing-admin seed update branch all passed runtime check or source review.

success_rate.backend: 83% (15/18 distinct assertions passed; all core requested reminder and regression flows passed, with 2 new-field validation failures and 1 CORS security failure)

seed_data_creation: Created temporary API and Mongo-seeded TEST_ intakes for in-window, out-of-window, missing-email, manual reminder, legacy, and invalid-input cases; created temporary cron-run and lockout rows. Cleanup fixtures removed all temporary intakes, cron runs, and login-attempt rows. Successful manual and cron checks sent reminder emails to the configured admin test address.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core reminder behavior is green. Manual success persisted reminder_sent_at and reminder_email_id. Cron auth returned 401 without/wrong Bearer, fresh delivery returned {accepted:true,run_id}, duplicate X-Webhook-Id returned duplicate:true, and only the pending in-window intake with email was updated. Requested /auth/me, /entries, /journal-presets, /alerts/status, commission-alerts cron, and delivery-bounces cron regressions passed. Re-run test_iteration21.py after adding validation/timezone normalization and CORS credential support.
rca_of_the_issue: IntakeCreateIn declares the new fields as Optional[str], and create_intake strips/stores them without semantic validation. The cron later relies on lexicographic string ranges and an '@' check, so malformed or non-canonical values are silently skipped and timezone-naive values are interpreted against UTC. Separately, CORSMiddleware is hardcoded to wildcard/no-credentials rather than using the configured explicit origin, which conflicts with cookie authentication.
